binding_note: r0 (message_reactions) is bound to r1 (messages) via message_id, r1 to r2 (channels) via channel_id, r2 to r3 (teams) via team_id, and r4 (user_teams) to r3 via team_id — all identifying that the reacted-to message sits in #core-infra within Test Workspace. The reaction's contributor (r0.user_id) is explicitly bound to the same person as r4.user_id, so the workspace_membership row r4 must belong to the reactor themselves, with role=admin; this equality is added explicitly per the exposure qualification and is not implied by team_id alone. No further relation is followed from that participant.

obligations.name: admin_eyes_reactions_core_infra
obligations.description: Select reactions where the reacting user's own workspace_membership role in Test Workspace is admin, the reaction_type is 'eyes', and the reacted message's channel is #core-infra; used to answer the user's question about which such reactions exist. No reaction in the environment satisfies all three conditions together.
obligations.scope: Reactions by workspace-admin members with emoji 'eyes' on messages posted in the #core-infra channel of Test Workspace

task_spec.text: Identify any reactions meeting the criteria and report which ones (if any) qualify, along with the reacting admin and the reacted message.

access_plan: Use conversations.list (or users.conversations) to locate the #core-infra channel ID within Test Workspace, then users.list/users.info to determine which members hold the admin workspace_membership role. Use conversations.history on #core-infra to enumerate its messages, then reactions.get on each message to check for 'eyes' reactions (name/user only, no timestamp exposed) and cross-reference each reacting user's own admin status; confirm no reaction satisfies all three conditions simultaneously.
